_comment: Labeled retrieval fixture for scripts/eval-retrieval.mjs. Documents and queries are drawn from this repository's real Doco-domain content (ADRs, auth flow, workflow rules, search architecture) so the harness exercises representative agent traffic. `relevant` is a list of document ids, or an object of { id: gain } for graded nDCG. Replace with exported Doco nodes once the Doco handle resolves.

documents.text: ADR-052: vector embeddings live behind a pluggable EmbeddingProvider interface with modelId, dimensions, and embed(). The default is a no-op (FTS only); when OPENAI_API_KEY is set the OpenAI text-embedding-3-small provider with 1536 dimensions is used. Self-hosted deployments add their own provider class.

ADR-049: the deployment is at Tier B scale, where sequential cosine similarity over every embedding in a Doco runs in microseconds. pgvector with ivfflat or hnsw indexes is an additive optimization deferred to Tier C; it is not needed yet.

Embeddings are stored in the embeddings table as bytea: the raw Float32Array bytes, little-endian, one row per entity. This is the same on-disk shape as the old SQLite blob, so a future swap to pgvector's vector(N) type is a column-type migration with no data reformat.

Agent queries are short natural-language questions while the corpus is dense typed prose, so retrieval is an asymmetric query-versus-document match. Instruction-tuned models that accept an input_type (query or document), such as Voyage and Cohere, outperform symmetric general-purpose embeddings on this shape.

A cross-encoder reranker reads the query and document together and resolves distinctions a single cosine score blurs. Running a reranker such as Cohere rerank-3.5 or Voyage rerank-2.5 over the hybrid top-K is the largest precision-at-k lever for natural-language retrieval.

Contextual retrieval prepends a short generated blurb situating each chunk in the whole document before embedding, which substantially reduces failed retrievals. It pairs well with hybrid lexical-plus-vector search and a reranker on a small high-value corpus.

Search is hybrid: a dense vector cosine score, Postgres full-text search over a weighted tsvector with English stemming, and a global PageRank centrality signal computed over the Doco's edge graph. Cross-category search is a union over the per-type FTS tables.

Agents authenticate to a Doco over OAuth 2.1. Shell-capable agents use the localhost-loopback flow; chat-only or sandboxed agents use the RFC 8628 device authorization grant, where the project owner approves the device code at doco.to/device. Both end with an Authorization Bearer token.

A read-only project token is a committable credential stored in .doco/project-tokens.json that lets any agent cloning the repo read the Doco without an interactive OAuth approval. The owner mints it from the project-tokens page after confirming repo readers may read the Doco.

For UI testing against production, POST a reserved test username such as doco-test-harness to /auth/dev-signin to obtain a doco_session cookie, then drive doco.to with that cookie. Any non-reserved username returns 403.

Every task that introduces commits must land in main before the turn ends. main is push-protected, so the path is: commit on a feature branch, open a pull request, mark it ready, and squash-merge it into main. Opening a draft PR and stopping is not done.

Every turn that touches the Doco renders an indicator at the top of the first text output, footer lines verbatim after any write, and a tally line at the very end reporting how many nodes were added or updated per source.
